ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
In the fourth quadrant of the Cartesian coordinate system $xOy$, there is a point $P(a, -b)$. A negatively charged particle with mass $m$ and charge magnitude $q$ (neglecting gravity) is projected from the origin $O$ with an initial velocity $v_{0}$ along the positive $y$-axis. A uniform magnetic field is applied perpendicular to the plane of the paper and directed inward throughout the coordinate system. The charge is able to pass exactly through the point $P$.

1. What is the magnitude of the magnetic induction of this uniform magnetic field?
2. If the velocity of the charged particle is changed to the $+x$ direction, and the magnetic field is replaced with a uniform electric field pointing vertically upward, such that the charged particle also passes through point $P$, what is the magnitude of the electric field strength?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a rectangular coordinate system, with the x-axis pointing to the right, the y-axis pointing upward, and the origin as O; the initial velocity v0 is along the positive y direction; point P is marked in the fourth quadrant, with coordinates P(a,-b), and dashed lines are used to indicate its projections to the x-axis and y-axis directions. Reasoning: The magnetic field is perpendicular to the paper surface inward, the particle carries negative charge, and the initial velocity is along +y, so the initial Lorentz force points to +x, and the center of the circular motion is in the positive direction of the x-axis, set as C(R,0). O and P are both on the circle, so CO=CP, namely R^2=(a-R)^2+b^2. Expanding gives 2aR=a^2+b^2, therefore R=(a^2+b^2)/(2a). The radius of circular motion in the magnetic field satisfies R=mv0/(qB), so B=mv0/(qR)=2amv0/[q(a^2+b^2)]. Electric field case: The initial velocity is changed to +x, the electric field is vertically upward, the negative charge is acted on by a force vertically downward, and the magnitude of acceleration is qE/m. The horizontal direction is uniform motion, x=v0t; when passing through P, x=a, so t=a/v0. The displacement in the vertical direction is -b, hence b=(1/2)(qE/m)t^2. Substituting t=a/v0 gives E=2bmv0^2/(qa^2).
